findings.fact: _wcsicmp_l loads unsigned16-bit units, applies ASCII A-Z+32 in C, otherwise calls exported _towlower_l separately on each unit, advances by2 and returns first mapped-unit difference. It does not decode supplementary scalars.
_wcslwr directly uses terminated ASCII A-Z+32 on its unchanged-locale fast path; otherwise calls _wcslwr_s_l with size_t(-1), then returns the original buffer pointer.

The private whole-lower helper uses terminated ASCII in C; nonzero locale issues two mapping-helper calls with flags0x100 and sourceCount-1, allocates temporary output and copies it back only on a successful mapping path.

The raw _wcslwr pointer return alone does not prove the private secure helper had no error; the original wrapper ignores that error code. Captured Success/LowerFailures describe public pointer results and guarded output values, not errno or every internal allocation/mapping outcome.

scope: Supports separate value-operation algorithms. This review does not claim parity for errno/invalid-parameter handlers, every possible whole-buffer context, other locales/runtime versions, original current locale or document/PC/physical behavior.
